title: Granite Trust - Data Residency & Compliance Discovery
summary: Initial discovery focused on data residency requirements across US/EU, HIPAA scope for a small fintech product, and options between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Customer needs SOC2/ISO artifacts, KMS/HSM integration, logging retention controls, and a timeline for procurement and pilot.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
GDPR & data residency for EU customers
Logging and audit log retention restrictions
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2 + ISO attestation and data residency docs by 2026-03-06
Schedule technical deep-dive with engineering (SE-led) the week of 3/9
Provide Dedicated pricing and RU/throughput estimates
Customer to share compliance questionnaire and primary use-cases (HIPAA/PII examples)
action_items: Avery Cole - Send SOC2 + ISO artifacts - 2026-03-06
Samir Patel - Schedule SE deep-dive and prepare benchmark plan - 2026-03-09
Priya Shah - Share compliance questionnaire and list of EU data flows - 2026-03-08
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Cole: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Avery from Redwood. we got Samir and Maya on the line too.
[00:04] Laura Peters: Hi, Laura here from Granite Trust, thanks for doing this. We've got Evan, Priya, and Mike as well.
[00:12] Avery Cole: Awesome; quick agenda — data residency, compliance controls (SOC2/ISO, HIPAA if needed), logging retention & PII handling, and then next steps. do I miss anything Evan?
[00:20] Evan Morales: Nope that's good. our main ask up front is — can Redwood Hosted be used for EU customer data, or do we need Dedicated or Private? and what does the audit trail look like.
[00:30] Samir Patel: Totally. high level: Hosted supports region pinning — we have EU regions for inference — but for strong data residency (legal & contractual) customers often prefer Redwood Dedicated or Private where the customer data and logs remain on isolated capacity.
[00:42] Priya Shah: Can you clarify "region pinning"? if we use Hosted, are logs or request metadata ever replicated to US infra?
[00:50] Samir Patel: Good question. For Hosted with EU pinning, model inference and token data processed in EU. however some control-plane metadata (billing, support traces) can be in US. for GDPR we're seeing customers want explicit contractual guarantees and data processing addenda — that's where Dedicated/Private is cleaner.
[01:06] Laura Peters: From a compliance perspective we need to know where raw prompts and embeddings are stored; we have PHI in a subset of flows so HIPAA is also on the table.
[01:16] Jordan Ruiz: When you say PHI in flows, is it persistent storage or ephemeral call-by-call?
[01:22] Mike Donnelly: It's a mix. core banking chat has account numbers occasionally and some support notes. most of it is transient but some records get stored in our data lake for analytics.
[01:32] Samir Patel: Important distinction. Redwood can be configured to not persist request bodies on Hosted if you opt out of logging; Dedicated gives you control over retention and can integrate with your S3/Blob in the same region. Private (on-prem/VPC) keeps everything in your network.
[01:46] Priya Shah: KMS integration — do you support customer-managed keys or HSM? we need keys we control for encryption-at-rest and for tokenization.
[01:54] Samir Patel: Yes, Dedicated and Private support customer-managed K M S — we integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and cloud HSMs. on Hosted we offer encryption but typically with Redwood-managed keys unless there's an enterprise contract.
[02:05] Laura Peters: Audit logs — what do they look like? retention windows and the ability to redact PII from logs?
[02:12] Maya Lin: Our audit logs include request id, timestamp, model/version, route, and per-request metadata. Raw prompts can be omitted on Dedicated/Private by configuration. We can redact or redact-at-ingest, but automated PII redaction isn't perfect — we recommend an app-layer scrub for PHI first.
[02:28] Evan Morales: So for HIPAA, we'd need logging that doesn't contain PHI or else encrypted logs with keys we control. can Redwood provide that?
[02:36] Samir Patel: Yes — two paths: 1) don't persist prompts at all in your Dedicated/Private deployment; 2) persist but encrypt with customer KMS and have strict RBAC + SIEM integration. both are supported.
[02:46] Priya Shah: Network isolation — if we go Dedicated, do we get VPC peering? how's private connectivity handled?
[02:52] Jordan Ruiz: Dedicated supports VPC endpoints and peering; Private can be deployed in your VPC or on-prem. we also have transit gateway options for large customers. small note: initial setup for VPC peering takes some networking work from both sides.
[03:04] Laura Peters: GDPR — data subject requests (DSR). If an EU user requests deletion, can we correlate requests to stored prompts/embeddings and delete them?
[03:12] Samir Patel: On Dedicated/Private yes — because you control storage mapping and we provide APIs to delete artifacts. On Hosted it's harder unless you have specific contract terms; we can build DSR flows but it's less standard.
[03:24] Mike Donnelly: Any constraints about model weights or serving? can models be hosted in EU as well?
[03:30] Samir Patel: Models can be served from EU region — we verify model artifacts and compile them into the runtime per region. note: some third-party model licenses restrict redistribution; that matters if you want a specific commercial model in-region.
[03:42] Evan Morales: Let's talk threat model briefly — where are logs stored and who can access them at Redwood?
[03:48] Maya Lin: Access is role-based; support access is audited. For Dedicated/Private, logs can be routed to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) and we can flip off support access to raw prompts if required.
[03:58] Laura Peters: Do you have SOC2 and ISO certs we can review?
[04:02] Avery Cole: Yes, we'll send SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestation after the call — I'll add that to next steps.
[04:08] Priya Shah: Regarding latency — if we choose Dedicated in EU, expected 99th percentile latency for conversational workloads? we need under 300ms for interactive agents.
[04:16] Samir Patel: Depends on model/sequence length; with our continuous batching and optimized kernels we often hit sub-200ms p99 for small context models on Dedicated pools. we'll propose a benchmark plan.
[04:28] Mike Donnelly: Pricing — curious about cost diff between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[04:32] Avery Cole: Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated involves reserved capacity (monthly commit) and predictable RU-based pricing; Private has platform fee + support. We'll send a pricing sketch.
[04:40] Evan Morales: Procurement timeline — assume security review and legal review. our procurement says 6-8 weeks for vendor questionnaires. can Redwood support a quick POC in parallel?
[04:48] Jordan Ruiz: Yes, we do short pilots. Usually SE-run benchmark with sample data in a restricted EU Dedicated pool or Private trial. we'll propose a 2-4 week pilot plan.
[04:58] Laura Peters: One more — embedding storage. We use embeddings for similarity search and customer data may include PII. can embeddings be tokenized or redacted?
[05:06] Samir Patel: Embeddings are stored as vectors; they can be encrypted at rest and scoped to your tenancy. semantic redaction is tough — best practice is to scrub PII before generating embeddings or store mapping metadata separately in your DB and encrypt it.
[05:20] Priya Shah: Any constraints on exporting logs for e-discovery or legal hold?
[05:24] Maya Lin: We can export logs to your S3 in-region and hold per retention policies. For legal hold we can extend retention on Dedicated/Private.
[05:32] Mike Donnelly: Are there any gotchas with KV cache and private deployments? we've heard KV cache can leak prefixes between tenants.
[05:38] Samir Patel: Good flag. Our runtime isolates KV caches per customer; in Dedicated with shared nodes we keep tenant isolation; Private gives you isolated nodes entirely. historically mis-attributions happen when caching config is wrong, but we have tests and can disable cross-tenant caching.
[05:54] Evan Morales: How does SSO/SAML and RBAC work for admin access? we need SCIM and SAML for provisioning.
[05:59] Avery Cole: We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC in Enterprise. Private deployments can hook into your IdP directly.
[06:06] Laura Peters: On the legal side, do you do Data Processing Addendums (DPA) that specify EU processing, sub-processors, and deletion guarantees?
[06:13] Avery Cole: Yes, standard DPA with EU data processing clauses is available. For Dedicated/Private we can negotiate tighter terms.
[06:20] Priya Shah: If we need HSM-backed keys on-prem, can Redwood's Private deployment talk to our HSM?
[06:26] Jordan Ruiz: Yes — in Private we can integrate with your HSM via network, or the deployment can be on your hardware with direct access. we'll need architecture review.
[06:34] Mike Donnelly: What's the typical implementation timeline for Private?
[06:37] Samir Patel: Private can take 8-12 weeks depending on procurement, network setup, and onboarding. Dedicated is usually 4-6 weeks. Hosted is immediate.
[06:46] Laura Peters: For the POC we'd like an SE-run benchmark with synthetically redacted PHI and a compliance checklist completed.
[06:53] Samir Patel: We'll prepare that. we'll also include recommended prompt redaction patterns and a sample scrub pipeline.
[06:58] Avery Cole: Alright let's recap next steps: we (Redwood) will send SOC2/ISO and DPA, Dedicated pricing and pilot plan, and schedule the SE deep-dive. Granite Trust to send compliance questionnaire and sample data flows. Any other items?
[07:12] Priya Shah: Also please include network runbook and VPC peering checklist in the docs.
[07:16] Avery Cole: Great — noted. thanks everyone. we'll follow up by Friday.
[07:20] Laura Peters: Thanks all.
[07:22] Evan Morales: Thanks.
[07:24] [Call ends]
